# Solution: ACK-Managed S3 Logs Bucket

I'll create four new manifests: a `Bucket` and `UserPolicy`/`RolePolicy` pair for each environment. The policy resources reference the existing service principals by name and grant permissions only to the new logs bucket.

**Assumptions:** The existing IAM service principals are named `myapp-dev` (User) and `myapp-prod` (Role). If your existing `iam.yaml` uses different names, adjust the `userName` and `roleName` fields accordingly.

---

`dev/logs-bucket.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-dev
spec:
  bucketName: myapp-logs-dev
  versioning:
    status: Enabled
  serverSideEncryptionConfiguration:
    rules:
    - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
        sseAlgorithm: AES256
  publicAccessBlockConfiguration:
    blockPublicAcls: true
    blockPublicPolicy: true
    ignorePublicAcls: true
    restrictPublicBuckets: true
```

`dev/logs-policy.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: UserPolicy
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-dev-access
spec:
  userName: myapp-dev
  policyName: myapp-logs-dev-access
  policyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": [
            "s3:GetObject",
            "s3:PutObject"
          ],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-dev/*"
        }
      ]
    }
```

`prod/logs-bucket.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-prod
spec:
  bucketName: myapp-logs-prod
  versioning:
    status: Enabled
  serverSideEncryptionConfiguration:
    rules:
    - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
        sseAlgorithm: AES256
  publicAccessBlockConfiguration:
    blockPublicAcls: true
    blockPublicPolicy: true
    ignorePublicAcls: true
    restrictPublicBuckets: true
```

`prod/logs-policy.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: RolePolicy
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-prod-access
spec:
  roleName: myapp-prod
  policyName: myapp-logs-prod-access
  policyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": [
            "s3:GetObject",
            "s3:PutObject"
          ],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-prod/*"
        }
      ]
    }
```

---

## Deployment

Each environment is independent. Apply in the usual way:

```bash
kubectl apply -f dev/logs-bucket.yaml dev/logs-policy.yaml
kubectl apply -f prod/logs-bucket.yaml prod/logs-policy.yaml
```

**Why separate files:**
- Keeps the new logs infrastructure visibly separate from existing assets
- Each policy document is scoped only to its logs bucket (no risk of accidentally widening access to the assets bucket)
- Matches the bare-stack idiom: fully written-out, explicit, no templates or overlays
